overview: Maori society comprises distinct iwi and hapu with their own histories and authority. This card introduces shared themes while preserving those differences. The imported map interval is not an extinction date: Maori communities, language and cultural institutions continue.

items.text: Growers adapted horticulture to a cooler climate, using techniques including stone walls and warmed soils to cultivate kumara. Practices varied with local environments.
Pounamu and obsidian supplied tool materials; harakeke supplied fibre. Gift exchange helped move valued materials among communities.
Local groups exercised their own authority. Genealogy connected individuals to wider communities, while tapu and mana shaped relationships with people and natural resources.
For many iwi, the midwinter appearance of Matariki marked the new year. Observances differ among iwi and include remembering the dead and sharing the harvest.
Carving, weaving and language revitalisation continued through the twentieth century. Maori communities developed language nests, broadcasting and new work in music, film and art.
